text:
cheng: heads-up: new AWQ act-quant bundle on canary started showing short truncation/early-eos under sustained traffic. dropping this thread for triage.
rita: paste config + any representative logs? :eyes:
sam: are we seeing perf regressions or strictly quality/decoding errors?
cheng: config snapshot:
```
model: llama-2-13b-awq
quant_backend: awq
group_size: 12
act_clip: 1.5
batcher:
  max_group: 64
  prefer_latency: true
route_policy: canary(3)
```
cheng: symptoms: frequent prefix-cache-miss spikes, then occasional early_eos (stream cut) around tail tokens on a subset of requests. example log lines:
```
[2026-09-12T14:33:02Z] req=az23 prefix_cache: miss group=12 seq=1
[2026-09-12T14:33:02Z] req=az23 kv_copy: allocated 0.45ms
[2026-09-12T14:33:02Z] req=az23 decode: early_eos detected at token 124
```
kevin: early_eos aligned with group boundary transitions? suspect act-quant scaling interacting with group padding -> low-energy signals getting clipped
maya: sounds like the hysteresis effect we noted in the quant paper notes — small per-group shifts that accumulate during autoregressive decode
rita: can you reproduce locally with a fixed prompt set? what do eval deltas vs fp16 look like?
cheng: ran a 1k-sample conversational QA eval. deltas vs fp16 baseline:
- accuracy-style metric: -0.72%
- ROUGE-L (chat): -0.9
- perplexity: +1.12
- early_eos rate: 0.6% baseline -> 2.1% on canary
sam: so both quality and early_eos regress under load. latency?
cheng: p50 ~ unchanged; p95 +8ms with group=12 & act_clip=1.5. also see more kv-copy jitter when QPS ramps
kevin: experiment proposal: reduce group_size -> 8, increase act_clip to 2.5, enable kv_prefetch to reduce cache misses
maya: alternate: keep group=12 and sweep act_clip: [1.0,1.25,1.5,1.75,2.0,2.5] and measure early_eos + accuracy deltas
cheng: ran a quick overnight sweep. summary:
- act_clip=1.0: acc -0.9%, early_eos 2.7%
- act_clip=1.5: acc -0.72%, early_eos 2.1% (current)
- act_clip=2.0: acc -0.3%, early_eos 1.4%
- act_clip=2.5: acc -0.12%, early_eos 1.1% but p95 +12ms and token compute cost +3%
rita: raising clip helps reduce clipping-driven early_eos but increases latency and unit compute. probably falling back to heavier kernels for some ops
sam: that's a trade-off we can accept if the quality delta is large. need cost/latency impact quantified for customers
cheng: cost delta ~+3% token-cost at act_clip 2.5 due to more FP-like dynamic range hitting slower compute path in some kernels
kevin: also validate across heterogenous group batching (mix of short and long seqs). padding/alignment affects activation distribution
maya: infra question — what's the canary rollout and auto-rollback thresholds? @infra-bot
infra-bot: canary(3) currently 5% traffic across two racks; auto-rollback if early_eos incidents exceed baseline + 0.5% over 30m or error-rate >0.2%
cheng: current numbers violate rollback threshold (2.1% vs baseline 0.6% => delta 1.5%)
rita: propose mitigations for canary: 1) reduce group_size -> 8 2) bump act_clip -> 2.0 3) enable kv_prefetch 4) increase canary evaluation window to 1h for stability
sam: agree. also add a smoke test of 10k focused prompts before any ramp-up that checks early_eos and top-k fidelity
cheng: pushed a quick override patch for the canary rollout:
```
{
  "route_policy": "canary(3)",
  "overrides": {
    "group_size": 8,
    "act_clip": 2.0,
    "kv_prefetch": true
  }
}
```
deploy-bot: deploy queued: rollout id r-20260912-az23, estimated ramp 20m -> 5% steady
maya: console suggestion: show early_eos rate per-route and a delta chart for act_clip sweeps in the Optimize UI
rita: also capture token-level entropy distributions pre/post quant to see if clipping shifts tail mass (could explain early_eos)
cheng: running entropy dumps + act_clip sweep capture now; will post gist with CSVs and sample histograms
sam: once the adjusted canary is steady, we should write a short playbook: "AWQ act-quant hysteresis: symptoms, mitigations, and rollout checklist"
kevin: add note about deterministic grouping vs dynamic grouping. our sims showed deterministic grouping reduced these boundary effects in some cases
maya: monitoring: watch early_eos delta and kv-copy latency. ping me if we cross thresholds. :party_parrot:
cheng: updated: gist with histograms uploaded https://gist.github.com/redwood-inference/aa33f2 (contains act_clip sweep CSVs + entropy dumps)
rita: reviewed gist. act_clip=2.0 looks like a good compromise — lower early_eos with acceptable latency. plan to re-run a 10k prompt smoke before wider rollout tomorrow
sam: thanks all. closing thread after follow-up validation tomorrow. :thumbsup:
